emailSubject: FMB News | LEDAC Approves 33 Priority Measures to Lower Cost of Living | August 9, 2026 | 6:00 AM PHT
headline: LEDAC Sets 33 Bills for Priority Passage in the 20th Congress
kicker: Congress · Common Legislative Agenda · Public policy
deck: The Legislative-Executive Development Advisory Council listed 33 bills for priority passage under the Common Legislative Agenda for the 20th Congress as of August 6.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: The Legislative-Executive Development Advisory Council listed 33 bills for priority passage under the Common Legislative Agenda for the 20th Congress as of August 6, according to the official LEDAC record and the Philippine News Agency.

sections.heading: What we know
paragraphs: The priority list includes an anti-political dynasty law, party-list system reform, freedom of information, amendments to the Bank Deposits Secrecy Law, a general tax amnesty, travel-tax abolition and amendments to the rice tariffication and downstream oil industry deregulation laws.

It also covers proposed changes to the Electric Power Industry Reform Act, education and nutrition measures, child online protection, assistance for people in crisis, infrastructure planning and agriculture and fisheries reforms.

The official Common Legislative Agenda separately identifies 25 other bills and two measures already enacted. A place on the priority list does not mean that a proposal has already passed Congress or become law.

sections.heading: Background
paragraphs: LEDAC is a consultative and advisory body that coordinates executive and legislative priorities on programs and policies requiring congressional action. The current agenda is for the 20th Congress, not the 19th Congress.

sections.heading: What remains unclear
paragraphs: Committee calendars and target floor dates for each of the 33 priority bills have not been published in one consolidated timetable. Each proposal must still complete the applicable legislative stages unless it has already done so.

sections.heading: Why this matters
paragraphs: The agenda covers household concerns including food and fuel prices, electricity charges, taxes, education, social protection and government transparency. The eventual effect depends on the final text approved by both chambers and signed into law.

sections.heading: What happens next
paragraphs: The House of Representatives and the Senate may prioritize committee work and plenary deliberations on the listed measures. Differences between chamber versions would still need to be reconciled before a bill can be sent to the President.
